While the story establishes a strong, atmospheric setting and introduces a cast of characters on the ferry, the elements do not ultimately come together to form a unified or satisfying whole. Most of the narrative is spent describing the routine of the ferry crossing and the three passengers (Wessel, the young woman, and Hahn), none of whom actually connect to or impact the central conflict introduced at the very end—the mysterious phone call from "Jonas." Because the story abruptly ends on this unexplained phone call without connecting it to the preceding character descriptions or resolving the tension, the narrative feels disjointed and incomplete rather than a harmonious whole where the beginning sets up the middle and logically leads to the end.
